transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I guess the main thing is that I just... I’ve stopped caring about everything I used to really look forward to. Like, my fishing gear is just sitting untouched out in the garage. I really need to clean that garage out, actually. The guys at work—I manage construction sites—they keep asking if they can borrow my power washer that's buried in there, and I keep telling them I'll dig it out. Supply chain issues have been backing up all our equipment deliveries lately, so everyone's trying to do things themselves... it's a whole mess downtown with the new commercial build. We had a concrete pour delayed three times last week. 

But, um, what was I saying? Right, the house. Even going into my woodshop just feels like a massive chore now. And when my kids try to get me to play chess with them... I sit down at the board, but I’m really just going through the motions. My youngest is actually getting pretty good at the Sicilian Defense, he watched some video on it, but I just... I can't get into it anymore.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, lately?

Down? I... I don't really know if I'd call it depressed. I'm not sure. I haven't really noticed feeling much of anything, honestly. It's more like I'm just dragging myself around, like my boots are full of wet cement. 

Which, actually, we finally got that delayed pour done on Thursday, but the mix was completely wrong. The supplier tried to blame the humidity, but I know for a fact they shorted us on the Portland cement. You can always tell by the color when it starts to cure. I've been doing this for twenty years, you can't pull a fast one on me with a bad mix. The site owner was furious, of course, breathing down my neck all morning. He drives this ridiculously clean truck to the site... never gets a speck of mud on the tires. I don't even know how that's possible in this weather, the access road is basically a swamp right now. 

But, um... sorry, I completely lost my train of thought. What did you just ask me?
Have you lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy, like fishing or working in your woodshop?

Yeah, I mean... exactly that. I just don't care about any of it anymore. The fishing gear is just gathering dust out there. Which reminds me, I really need to get the garage door fixed. The track got bent when my wife backed her car into it last winter. It's a miracle the glass didn't shatter. She drives this old Subaru, you know, the ones from the early 2000s that run forever? We’ve put like two hundred thousand miles on that thing. The mechanic says the head gasket is going to blow any day now, but she refuses to trade it in. She says it has character. 

But yeah, the woodshop... it just feels like work now. A chore. And the kids, they keep setting up the chessboard, but I just stare at the pieces. I'm just going through the motions. I think my oldest is starting to notice, he asked me the other day if I was mad at him. I wasn't mad, I just... I don't know. Did I answer your question?
Have you been feeling down or sad most of the day, nearly every day, lately?

Sad? I don't... I wouldn't say sad. I just feel heavy. Like I said, like I'm dragging myself through wet cement. Which is funny, because I actually had to fire a guy yesterday for tracking wet cement into the site office. Just walked right in with his boots caked in it, ruined the carpet. Not that it was a nice carpet, it's one of those cheap industrial ones, the gray kind with the little blue flecks in it? We got it on discount from a supplier over in Westlake. They were liquidating their whole warehouse because the owner decided to retire and move to Florida. Tampa, I think. Or maybe Sarasota. Somewhere on the Gulf Coast. He always talked about wanting to buy a boat and just fish all day. 

I don't know why anyone would want to fish in the ocean, though. Too much salt, ruins your gear if you don't wash it right away. 

But, uh... wait, what were we talking about? Did you ask about the site office?
Have you been feeling down or sad most of the day, nearly every day, lately?

I... I thought we just went over this? I mean, I'm not really sad, just... empty, I guess. Numb. It's just this constant weight, you know? Like the load-bearing walls in that new commercial build we're doing downtown. 

Speaking of which, the structural engineer on that project is a complete nightmare. He keeps changing the specs on the steel beams. Every time we order them, he revises the blueprints. It's costing us a fortune in delays. And steel prices are through the roof right now anyway, ever since those new tariffs went into effect. My brother-in-law, he works in logistics, he says the shipping containers are just sitting at the port for weeks because they can't get enough truck drivers to move them. It's a whole supply chain mess. He actually bought a new rig last year, a Peterbilt. Beautiful truck, cherry red. 

But, um... sorry. I'm doing it again, aren't I? Just rambling. You were asking if I felt sad? I really don't think sad is the right word. I just don't feel much of anything.
Have you felt this way—like you're dragging yourself through wet cement or carrying a constant weight—every day for the past two weeks or more?

Yeah... yeah, it's definitely been more than two weeks. It's been, gosh, about a year and seven months now. Ever since my wife's health problems started and everything at home just... changed. 

Which, honestly, getting her to go to the doctor in the first place was a battle. She's so stubborn. Reminds me of her father, actually. He used to refuse to go to the dentist, even when he had this terrible toothache. Ended up needing a root canal, and they had to put a crown on it. Gold crown, right in the back. He always joked that it was his retirement fund. He was a funny guy, worked at the post office for thirty years. He used to bring home all these stamps that had misprints on them. Apparently, those are worth a lot of money to collectors? Philatelists, I think they're called. I watched this documentary once about a guy who spent his entire life savings on this one rare stamp from British Guiana. Millions of dollars for a tiny piece of paper with some ink on it. Crazy what people will value, right? 

But, uh, anyway... yeah. A year and seven months. That's how long it's been like this.
Have you felt a depressed mood most of the day, nearly every day, for at least the past two weeks?

I feel like we're going in circles here, doc. Depressed? I... I don't really use that word. Like I keep saying, it's just heavy. Empty. When you say depressed, my brain just goes to, like, a physical depression. Like a dip in a foundation. 

We actually had that happen on a pour last month. The sub-base wasn't compacted right because of all the rain, and we got this massive depression right in the middle of the concrete slab. Sank almost three inches. We had to hire this specialized crew to come out and drill holes, pump this high-density polyurethane foam underneath to lift it back up to level. Slabjacking, they call it. It's a fascinating process, really. The foreman running the pump, big guy named Hector, he had this massive scar across his chin from a motorcycle accident. Said he laid his Harley down on the interstate going seventy miles an hour. He still rides, though. I don't know how you get back on a bike after something like that. My wife's cousin bought a Vespa once to commute to his bakery, and somebody stole it the very first week. 

But... wait. Sorry. You were asking if I'm depressed? I just... I don't know if that's the right label. I just know the heavy feeling hasn't gone away.
Have you found that you no longer get any pleasure or satisfaction from activities that used to be important or enjoyable to you, like fishing or working in your woodshop?

Yeah, I guess... the main thing is that I just stopped caring about all of it. Everything I used to look forward to. My fishing gear is still sitting untouched in the garage from last summer. I haven't even checked the lines. 

And you know, speaking of the garage, I really need to reorganize that space. My neighbor, Dave, he just installed these overhead storage racks in his garage. Beautiful system, all heavy-duty steel. He bought them online from this company in Oregon. Apparently, the guy who started the company used to be an aerospace engineer for Boeing, and he just got tired of the corporate grind and started making garage racks. Dave said the shipping took forever, though, because of some strike at the freight company. I think it was the teamsters? My uncle was a teamster back in Chicago in the eighties. He used to tell these wild stories about the union bosses and the things they'd get away with. He had this massive collection of vintage union pins, kept them all in this velvet-lined display case he built himself. 

But, uh, anyway... the woodshop. Yeah, it just feels like a chore now. I go out there and just stare at the tools. Even when my kids try to get me to play chess, which we used to do every Sunday, I'm just... going through the motions. I don't really care who wins anymore.
Have you been blaming yourself for things more than usual, or feeling like you're not worth much lately?

I... yeah. I do. I just keep thinking I've completely failed my wife, my kids... even the guys at work. Like, if anything goes wrong at all—a missed doctor's appointment for my wife, a cost overrun on a job, a safety issue—I just take it as proof that I'm completely useless. 

Speaking of safety issues, we had this OSHA inspector show up unannounced on Tuesday. Guy walked onto the site wearing the cleanest boots I've ever seen. You can always tell a guy who doesn't actually work in the dirt by his boots. They were Red Wings, I think. Classic moc toe. I used to wear Red Wings back when I was just starting out as a framing carpenter, but they take forever to break in. You have to rub mink oil into the leather every night for a week. My grandfather swore by mink oil. He used it on his baseball mitts, too. He played minor league ball for a couple of years in the fifties. Actually got to bat against Satchel Paige once in an exhibition game. Struck out on three pitches, but he talked about it until the day he died. He had this framed newspaper clipping of the box score hanging in his hallway right next to this awful velvet painting of a matador that my grandmother hated. She tried to throw it out during a garage sale in '98, but he caught her...

But, um... sorry. Where was I? The... blaming myself. Right. Yeah, every little mistake, every overrun or missed appointment, I just look at it and think everybody would be better off without me in charge. I'm just messing it all up.
Have you been feeling like you're a failure or that you've let people down more days than not lately?

I mean, yeah, like I was just saying... I just keep thinking I've completely failed everyone. My wife, my kids, the guys on the crew. It's like... more days than not? Yeah, definitely. Every single day, pretty much. If anything goes wrong—like that missed appointment for my wife, or a cost overrun, or a safety issue—I just take it as absolute proof that I'm completely useless. 

Like those cost overruns... lumber prices are just out of control right now. We had to re-quote this whole framing package for a custom build out in the suburbs because the price of OSB plywood jumped thirty percent in two weeks. Thirty percent! The client was furious. He's this retired orthodontist, drives a pristine 1960s Jaguar E-Type. Beautiful car, British racing green. My dad had a buddy who restored old British sports cars. He always said the Lucas electrical systems in those things were a nightmare. They used to call Lucas the "Prince of Darkness" because the headlights would just randomly cut out on the highway at night. He had a whole shelf in his garage just dedicated to spare fuses and wiring harnesses. He actually wired his own house, too, which I'm pretty sure wasn't up to code, but he never had an inspector out because he lived way out in the county. He had this massive garden out back where he grew these heirloom tomatoes...

Wait, sorry. The... letting people down. Yeah. I just... I look at all of it, every mistake, and I just think everybody would be better off without me in charge. I'm just dragging them all down.
Have you noticed a big drop in your energy level or felt unusually tired, even when you're not doing much?

Yeah, it's... I'm just so drained. All the time. By midmorning, I feel like I've already worked a full shift. Just walking the project or climbing the stairs with the crew, it feels like my whole body is carrying wet concrete. 

Which, you know, speaking of wet concrete, we had a massive foundation pour last Thursday that almost went completely sideways. The ready-mix trucks got stuck in traffic because of some huge wreck on the interstate. I heard it was a guy hauling a horse trailer who blew a tire. My cousin actually used to haul quarter horses down in Texas. He drove this massive Ford dually, custom paint job, dual exhaust. He practically lived on I-35. To stay awake on those long hauls, he'd listen to these old cassette tape audiobooks. Mostly Louis L'Amour westerns. He had boxes and boxes of them in his garage. His wife finally made him donate them to the library when they downsized a few years ago. They bought this little mid-century ranch house, beautiful original hardwood floors, but the foundation was settling on one side, so they had to get mudjacking done to level it out... 

But, um, anyway. Sorry. I keep doing that. My energy. Yeah, it's just gone. Even when I'm just sitting in the site trailer doing nothing, I just feel so heavy and unusually tired. Like I can barely lift my own legs.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight lately—like eating a lot less or more than usual, or losing or gaining weight without trying?

Yeah, my appetite is just... gone. Most days food just tastes like cardboard. I'll skip breakfast completely, and even if I've been out on a job site all day, I just end up picking at my dinner. My wife made this pot roast the other night, usually my favorite. She gets these really good cuts from this local butcher shop downtown. The guy who runs it is a third-generation butcher. His grandfather came over from Poland, I think. Or maybe Hungary. Anyway, they still use the original meat scales from the 1920s. Beautiful brass things, really heavy. You don't see craftsmanship like that anymore. Everything now is digital and made of cheap plastic that breaks in a year. We had a guy on the crew buy this cheap laser level off the internet, and the thing was out of plumb straight out of the box. Cost us a whole morning of framing before we caught it. You really get what you pay for with tools. My first boss always told me to buy the best hammer I could afford, because a cheap one will ruin your elbow. He had this titanium framing hammer...

But, sorry. Food. Right. Yeah, I just don't want to eat. And I've definitely lost weight without even trying to. I've had to bring my belt in a couple of notches lately just to keep my pants up.
Have you noticed that you're moving slower than usual, or that even simple tasks take you longer to finish than they used to?

I don't... I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean, I guess I'm tired, but moving slower? I don't think so. Simple tasks are just simple tasks. Like signing off on the daily logs. I still do that. My pen just sits right there on my desk in the trailer. It's this heavy brass pen my wife got me for our tenth anniversary. She had it engraved with my initials. The guy who did the engraving works out of this little kiosk in the mall, but he's actually a retired watchmaker. He was telling me once about how he used to repair these intricate Swiss movements. Tiny little gears, like, microscopic almost. You have to use these special magnifying loupes just to see what you're doing. He said the hardest part was keeping the dust out of the casing. Dust is just everywhere. Especially on a job site. We have to run these massive air scrubbers sometimes when we're doing drywall sanding, otherwise the whole place just looks like a snow globe. The filters on those things cost a fortune, and you have to change them out constantly or the motor burns out. We had a motor burn out on a compressor last month and the smell of the ozone was just... 

Anyway, what were you asking? Moving slower? No, I don't think I'm moving any slower than usual. It doesn't take me longer to do things, I just... I don't know, I just don't have the energy for them. But the speed is the same, I guess.
Have you felt like you're not worth much or that you've been overly critical of yourself lately?

Yeah, I... I definitely feel that way. A lot. I keep thinking I've just completely failed my wife, my kids, the guys at work. If anything goes wrong on a job—like a cost overrun, or a safety issue, or even just missing an appointment—I take it as absolute proof that I'm useless. That they'd all be better off without me in charge. 

Like, we had this safety inspection last month, OSHA showed up unannounced. The inspector was this young guy, probably fresh out of college, wearing a hard hat that looked like it had never seen a speck of dust. He was carrying one of those heavy-duty clipboards. The aluminum ones that open up so you can store paperwork inside. My dad used to have one of those when he was a dispatcher for a trucking company. He'd sit at this big metal desk covered in waybills and delivery manifests. He always used these specific blue ink pens, said black ink made it too easy for people to forge documents. He was really paranoid about that. He actually caught a guy once trying to alter a logbook to cover up some missing freight. Turned out it was a whole ring of guys stealing copper wire from the yard. Copper prices were through the roof back then. Still are, really. We have to lock up all the electrical spools on site in these massive steel job boxes, otherwise they walk off overnight. The locks on those boxes are supposed to be bolt-cutter proof, but I saw a video online where a guy picked one in under a minute using just a tension wrench and a rake pick...

But, yeah. Sorry. What was I saying? Right, feeling useless. It's just... I just feel like I'm letting everyone down, all the time. Like I'm just not worth much anymore.
Have you noticed any trouble focusing, making decisions, or thinking clearly lately?

Yeah, my focus is just totally shot. I used to be able to keep all the schedules and subcontractors straight right in my head, no problem. You have to, really, because if the plumbers get delayed, then the drywall guys are sitting around waiting, and then the painters... 

Speaking of painters, we had this crew last week using this new low-VOC paint. The environmental regulations now are just getting so strict. I mean, I get it, the fumes are bad for you, but this new stuff takes twice as long to cure. My uncle used to paint cars back in the 70s, custom hot rods and stuff. He used this heavy enamel paint that probably took ten years off his life just breathing it in. He had this vintage Mustang he painted candy apple red. Beautiful car. He actually traded a guy a set of golf clubs for it, if you can believe that. The clubs belonged to some semi-pro golfer who went bankrupt. Golf is such an expensive sport anyway, just the greens fees alone... my buddy Dave plays every Sunday at this course out by the lake. The lake has been really low this year, though. We haven't had nearly enough rain, and the docks are all just sitting in the mud...

But... sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, thinking clearly. Right. Yeah, it's bad. I'll literally sit at my desk and read the same email three times and have no idea what it said. I walk into site meetings and completely forget what I was even about to say. And decisions... I just freeze up. Things I used to make a call on in five minutes now just completely paralyze me. I just can't seem to get my brain to work right.

I feel like we're going in circles here, doc. Depressed? I... I don't really use that word. Like I keep saying, it's just heavy. Empty. When you say depressed, my brain just goes to, like, a physical depression. Like a dip in a foundation.

Sank almost three inches. We had to hire this specialized crew to come out and drill holes, pump this high-density polyurethane foam underneath to lift it back up to level. Slabjacking, they call it. It's a fascinating process, really. The foreman running the pump, big guy named Hector, he had this massive scar across his chin from a motorcycle accident. Said he laid his Harley down on the interstate going seventy miles an hour. He still rides, though. I don't know how you get back on a bike after something like that. My wife's cousin bought a Vespa once to commute to his bakery, and somebody stole it the very first week. 

But... wait. Sorry. You were asking if I'm depressed? I just... I don't know if that's the right label. I just know the heavy feeling hasn't gone away.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences a loss of pleasure in activities they once enjoyed, a key symptom of depression.
doctor.question: Have you found that you no longer get any pleasure or satisfaction from activities that used to be important or enjoyable to you, like fishing or working in your woodshop?

target_item.name: Loss_of_Interest
target_item.manifestation: I guess the main thing is that I just stopped caring about everything I used to look forward to—my fishing gear is still sitting untouched in the garage, the woodshop feels like a chore, and even when my kids try to get me to play chess I’m just going through the motions.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if I no longer get pleasure or satisfaction from activities I used to enjoy, specifically mentioning fishing and my woodshop, which directly aligns with the Loss_of_Interest symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Yeah, I guess... the main thing is that I just stopped caring about all of it. Everything I used to look forward to. My fishing gear is still sitting untouched in the garage from last summer. I haven't even checked the lines. 

And you know, speaking of the garage, I really need to reorganize that space. My neighbor, Dave, he just installed these overhead storage racks in his garage. Beautiful system, all heavy-duty steel. He bought them online from this company in Oregon. Apparently, the guy who started the company used to be an aerospace engineer for Boeing, and he just got tired of the corporate grind and started making garage racks. Dave said the shipping took forever, though, because of some strike at the freight company. I think it was the teamsters? My uncle was a teamster back in Chicago in the eighties. He used to tell these wild stories about the union bosses and the things they'd get away with. He had this massive collection of vintage union pins, kept them all in this velvet-lined display case he built himself. 

But, uh, anyway... the woodshop. Yeah, it just feels like a chore now. I go out there and just stare at the tools. Even when my kids try to get me to play chess, which we used to do every Sunday, I'm just... going through the motions. I don't really care who wins anymore.

inference.note: The patient has endorsed a persistently low mood (described as 'heavy,' 'empty,' and 'dragging through wet cement'), loss of interest in previously enjoyable activities (e.g., fishing, woodshop, playing chess), and symptoms lasting over two years (chronic). There is no mention of manic or hypomanic episodes, ruling out bipolar disorders. The duration and severity suggest either a moderate major depressive episode or persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia). The distinction between F32.2 and F33.2 hinges on duration and chronicity; both remain likely at this point.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt, which would support F32.2/F33.2, or if there is a lack of such symptoms, which may differentiate between the two.
doctor.question: Have you been blaming yourself for things more than usual, or feeling like you're not worth much lately?

target_item.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
target_item.manifestation: I keep thinking I’ve failed my wife, my kids, and the guys at work, and if anything goes wrong—a missed appointment, a cost overrun, a safety issue—I take it as proof that I’m useless and everyone would be better off without me in charge.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about feelings of worthlessness or excessive self-blame, which directly corresponds to the Worthlessness_Guilt symptom.

patient.answer:
I... yeah. I do. I just keep thinking I've completely failed my wife, my kids... even the guys at work. Like, if anything goes wrong at all—a missed doctor's appointment for my wife, a cost overrun on a job, a safety issue—I just take it as proof that I'm completely useless. 

Speaking of safety issues, we had this OSHA inspector show up unannounced on Tuesday. Guy walked onto the site wearing the cleanest boots I've ever seen. You can always tell a guy who doesn't actually work in the dirt by his boots. They were Red Wings, I think. Classic moc toe. I used to wear Red Wings back when I was just starting out as a framing carpenter, but they take forever to break in. You have to rub mink oil into the leather every night for a week. My grandfather swore by mink oil. He used it on his baseball mitts, too. He played minor league ball for a couple of years in the fifties. Actually got to bat against Satchel Paige once in an exhibition game. Struck out on three pitches, but he talked about it until the day he died. He had this framed newspaper clipping of the box score hanging in his hallway right next to this awful velvet painting of a matador that my grandmother hated. She tried to throw it out during a garage sale in '98, but he caught her...

But, um... sorry. Where was I? The... blaming myself. Right. Yeah, every little mistake, every overrun or missed appointment, I just look at it and think everybody would be better off without me in charge. I'm just messing it all up.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt, which would help confirm a diagnosis of major depressive disorder (F32.2 or F33.2).
doctor.question: Have you been feeling like you're a failure or that you've let people down more days than not lately?

target_item.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
target_item.manifestation: I keep thinking I’ve failed my wife, my kids, and the guys at work, and if anything goes wrong—a missed appointment, a cost overrun, a safety issue—I take it as proof that I’m useless and everyone would be better off without me in charge.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about feelings of being a failure and letting people down, which corresponds to the symptom of worthlessness and guilt.

patient.answer:
I mean, yeah, like I was just saying... I just keep thinking I've completely failed everyone. My wife, my kids, the guys on the crew. It's like... more days than not? Yeah, definitely. Every single day, pretty much. If anything goes wrong—like that missed appointment for my wife, or a cost overrun, or a safety issue—I just take it as absolute proof that I'm completely useless. 

Like those cost overruns... lumber prices are just out of control right now. We had to re-quote this whole framing package for a custom build out in the suburbs because the price of OSB plywood jumped thirty percent in two weeks. Thirty percent! The client was furious. He's this retired orthodontist, drives a pristine 1960s Jaguar E-Type. Beautiful car, British racing green. My dad had a buddy who restored old British sports cars. He always said the Lucas electrical systems in those things were a nightmare. They used to call Lucas the "Prince of Darkness" because the headlights would just randomly cut out on the highway at night. He had a whole shelf in his garage just dedicated to spare fuses and wiring harnesses. He actually wired his own house, too, which I'm pretty sure wasn't up to code, but he never had an inspector out because he lived way out in the county. He had this massive garden out back where he grew these heirloom tomatoes...

Wait, sorry. The... letting people down. Yeah. I just... I look at all of it, every mistake, and I just think everybody would be better off without me in charge. I'm just dragging them all down.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a significant decrease in energy or increased fatigue, which helps distinguish between major depressive disorder and persistent depressive disorder.
doctor.question: Have you noticed a big drop in your energy level or felt unusually tired, even when you're not doing much?

target_item.name: Fatigue
target_item.manifestation: By midmorning I feel like I’ve already worked a full shift, and even walking the project or climbing stairs with the crew feels like my body is carrying wet concrete.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a drop in energy level or feeling unusually tired, which directly matches the symptom of fatigue.

patient.answer:
Yeah, it's... I'm just so drained. All the time. By midmorning, I feel like I've already worked a full shift. Just walking the project or climbing the stairs with the crew, it feels like my whole body is carrying wet concrete. 

Which, you know, speaking of wet concrete, we had a massive foundation pour last Thursday that almost went completely sideways. The ready-mix trucks got stuck in traffic because of some huge wreck on the interstate. I heard it was a guy hauling a horse trailer who blew a tire. My cousin actually used to haul quarter horses down in Texas. He drove this massive Ford dually, custom paint job, dual exhaust. He practically lived on I-35. To stay awake on those long hauls, he'd listen to these old cassette tape audiobooks. Mostly Louis L'Amour westerns. He had boxes and boxes of them in his garage. His wife finally made him donate them to the library when they downsized a few years ago. They bought this little mid-century ranch house, beautiful original hardwood floors, but the foundation was settling on one side, so they had to get mudjacking done to level it out... 

But, um, anyway. Sorry. I keep doing that. My energy. Yeah, it's just gone. Even when I'm just sitting in the site trailer doing nothing, I just feel so heavy and unusually tired. Like I can barely lift my own legs.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a significant change in appetite or weight loss/gain, which is a key differentiator between persistent depressive disorder (F33.2) and major depressive disorder (F32.2).
doctor.question: Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight lately—like eating a lot less or more than usual, or losing or gaining weight without trying?

target_item.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
target_item.manifestation: Most days food tastes like cardboard, so I’ll skip breakfast and pick at dinner even if I’ve been on a job site all day, and my belt has had to come in a couple notches without me trying.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking about changes in appetite and weight, which corresponds to the Weight_Appetite_Change symptom.

patient.answer:
Yeah, my appetite is just... gone. Most days food just tastes like cardboard. I'll skip breakfast completely, and even if I've been out on a job site all day, I just end up picking at my dinner. My wife made this pot roast the other night, usually my favorite. She gets these really good cuts from this local butcher shop downtown. The guy who runs it is a third-generation butcher. His grandfather came over from Poland, I think. Or maybe Hungary. Anyway, they still use the original meat scales from the 1920s. Beautiful brass things, really heavy. You don't see craftsmanship like that anymore. Everything now is digital and made of cheap plastic that breaks in a year. We had a guy on the crew buy this cheap laser level off the internet, and the thing was out of plumb straight out of the box. Cost us a whole morning of framing before we caught it. You really get what you pay for with tools. My first boss always told me to buy the best hammer I could afford, because a cheap one will ruin your elbow. He had this titanium framing hammer...

But, sorry. Food. Right. Yeah, I just don't want to eat. And I've definitely lost weight without even trying to. I've had to bring my belt in a couple of notches lately just to keep my pants up.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences psychomotor agitation or retardation, which would support the diagnosis of major depressive disorder with melancholic features (F32.2) or persistent depressive disorder with melancholic features (F33.2).
doctor.question: Have you noticed that you're moving slower than usual, or that even simple tasks take you longer to finish than they used to?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about psychomotor retardation (moving slower than usual), which is not included in my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
I don't... I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean, I guess I'm tired, but moving slower? I don't think so. Simple tasks are just simple tasks. Like signing off on the daily logs. I still do that. My pen just sits right there on my desk in the trailer. It's this heavy brass pen my wife got me for our tenth anniversary. She had it engraved with my initials. The guy who did the engraving works out of this little kiosk in the mall, but he's actually a retired watchmaker. He was telling me once about how he used to repair these intricate Swiss movements. Tiny little gears, like, microscopic almost. You have to use these special magnifying loupes just to see what you're doing. He said the hardest part was keeping the dust out of the casing. Dust is just everywhere. Especially on a job site. We have to run these massive air scrubbers sometimes when we're doing drywall sanding, otherwise the whole place just looks like a snow globe. The filters on those things cost a fortune, and you have to change them out constantly or the motor burns out. We had a motor burn out on a compressor last month and the smell of the ozone was just... 

Anyway, what were you asking? Moving slower? No, I don't think I'm moving any slower than usual. It doesn't take me longer to do things, I just... I don't know, I just don't have the energy for them. But the speed is the same, I guess.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt, which would help differentiate between the two current diagnostic candidates.
doctor.question: Have you felt like you're not worth much or that you've been overly critical of yourself lately?

target_item.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
target_item.manifestation: I keep thinking I’ve failed my wife, my kids, and the guys at work, and if anything goes wrong—a missed appointment, a cost overrun, a safety issue—I take it as proof that I’m useless and everyone would be better off without me in charge.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question about feeling not worth much or being overly critical directly asks about feelings of worthlessness and guilt.

patient.answer:
Yeah, I... I definitely feel that way. A lot. I keep thinking I've just completely failed my wife, my kids, the guys at work. If anything goes wrong on a job—like a cost overrun, or a safety issue, or even just missing an appointment—I take it as absolute proof that I'm useless. That they'd all be better off without me in charge. 

Like, we had this safety inspection last month, OSHA showed up unannounced. The inspector was this young guy, probably fresh out of college, wearing a hard hat that looked like it had never seen a speck of dust. He was carrying one of those heavy-duty clipboards. The aluminum ones that open up so you can store paperwork inside. My dad used to have one of those when he was a dispatcher for a trucking company. He'd sit at this big metal desk covered in waybills and delivery manifests. He always used these specific blue ink pens, said black ink made it too easy for people to forge documents. He was really paranoid about that. He actually caught a guy once trying to alter a logbook to cover up some missing freight. Turned out it was a whole ring of guys stealing copper wire from the yard. Copper prices were through the roof back then. Still are, really. We have to lock up all the electrical spools on site in these massive steel job boxes, otherwise they walk off overnight. The locks on those boxes are supposed to be bolt-cutter proof, but I saw a video online where a guy picked one in under a minute using just a tension wrench and a rake pick...

But, yeah. Sorry. What was I saying? Right, feeling useless. It's just... I just feel like I'm letting everyone down, all the time. Like I'm just not worth much anymore.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a diminished ability to think or concentrate, which is relevant to differentiating between the two diagnosis candidates.
doctor.question: Have you noticed any trouble focusing, making decisions, or thinking clearly lately?

target_item.name: Diminished_Thinking
target_item.manifestation: I used to keep schedules and subcontractors straight in my head, but now I’ll read the same email three times, forget what I was about to say in meetings, and freeze over decisions I used to make in five minutes.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question about trouble focusing, making decisions, or thinking clearly maps directly to the Diminished_Thinking symptom.

patient.answer:
Yeah, my focus is just totally shot. I used to be able to keep all the schedules and subcontractors straight right in my head, no problem. You have to, really, because if the plumbers get delayed, then the drywall guys are sitting around waiting, and then the painters... 

Speaking of painters, we had this crew last week using this new low-VOC paint. The environmental regulations now are just getting so strict. I mean, I get it, the fumes are bad for you, but this new stuff takes twice as long to cure. My uncle used to paint cars back in the 70s, custom hot rods and stuff. He used this heavy enamel paint that probably took ten years off his life just breathing it in. He had this vintage Mustang he painted candy apple red. Beautiful car. He actually traded a guy a set of golf clubs for it, if you can believe that. The clubs belonged to some semi-pro golfer who went bankrupt. Golf is such an expensive sport anyway, just the greens fees alone... my buddy Dave plays every Sunday at this course out by the lake. The lake has been really low this year, though. We haven't had nearly enough rain, and the docks are all just sitting in the mud...

But... sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, thinking clearly. Right. Yeah, it's bad. I'll literally sit at my desk and read the same email three times and have no idea what it said. I walk into site meetings and completely forget what I was even about to say. And decisions... I just freeze up. Things I used to make a call on in five minutes now just completely paralyze me. I just can't seem to get my brain to work right.

inference.note: The patient has consistently described symptoms that meet criteria for major depressive disorder, with the persistence of symptoms for over two years suggesting a chronic course rather than a single episode. The absence of manic or hypomanic symptoms rules out bipolar disorder. The symptoms reported align with F33.2 (Recurrent Depressive Disorder, current episode severe without psychotic symptoms).
